module.purpose: Integration tests for round-robin lucky-user selection, including no-show handling, weighted ordering, monthly booking calibration, and host creation-date calibration against a Prisma database.
module.summary: This Vitest integration suite provisions event types, users, hosts, bookings, and attendees through Prisma, then exercises lucky-user selection and ordered-list selection. It verifies that no-show bookings are excluded or attributed correctly, weights and current-month booking counts influence ordering, prior-month bookings are ignored, and host creation timing affects calibration. Fake timers provide deterministic date-dependent behavior, while hooks isolate database fixtures between tests.
module.businessContext: The file protects Cal.com round-robin scheduling fairness and host allocation. Failures could assign bookings to the wrong host, violate weighting or calibration rules, or leak test data across integration cases.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A host with a later booking marked noShowHost competes with a host whose earlier booking was attended.
moduleContractTests.rationale: No-show host bookings must not count toward round-robin selection.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An organizer whose attendee is marked no-show competes with an organizer whose attendee attended.
moduleContractTests.then: await expect(getLuckyUser({ availableUsers, eventType, allRRHosts, routingFormResponse })).resolves.toStrictEqual(organizerWhoseAttendeeDidntShowUp)
moduleContractTests.rationale: Attendee no-show status determines whether the organizer booking contributes to round robin.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A fixed host booking has a no-show attendee corresponding to another round-robin host.
moduleContractTests.then: await expect(getLuckyUser({ availableUsers, eventType, allRRHosts, routingFormResponse })).resolves.toStrictEqual(organizerWhoWasAttendeeAndDidntShowUp)
moduleContractTests.rationale: Fixed-host no-show attendee bookings are attributed to the round-robin host who missed them.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Two hosts have bookings with noShowHost explicitly null and different creation times.
moduleContractTests.then: await expect(getLuckyUser({ availableUsers, eventType, allRRHosts, routingFormResponse })).resolves.toStrictEqual(userWithBookingThatHappenedEarlier)
moduleContractTests.rationale: Null no-show values represent ordinary bookings and must remain eligible for ordering.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Hosts have no bookings or distinguishing weight and are supplied in different availableUsers orders.
moduleContractTests.when: getOrderedListOfLuckyUsers({ availableUsers: [user2, user1, user3], eventType, allRRHosts, routingFormResponse })
moduleContractTests.rationale: With no ranking criteria, ordering follows the supplied available-user sequence.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Hosts with weights 100, 200, and 100 have no bookings while round-robin weights are enabled.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Higher host weight must rank ahead of equal-weight hosts.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Hosts with weights 200, 100, and 100 have one, two, and three current-month bookings.
given: bookings: [{ eventTypeId: commonEventTypeId, createdAt: new Date() }]
moduleContractTests.rationale: Current-month booking counts affect ranking and booking shortfall calibration.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Hosts have bookings only from the previous month and different weights.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Bookings outside the current month must not affect shortfalls or ranking.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Hosts created on the tenth, ninth, and eighth of the month have increasing booking counts.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Host creation timing contributes to calibration alongside weight and booking history.

detail.name: deleteUsers
preconditions: The shared user ID collection and Prisma user delegate are available.
postconditions: Prisma has been asked to delete all users whose IDs were in the tracked user ID collection at call time.
After successful deletion, the tracked user ID collection is empty.
invariants: Only users matching the tracked IDs are targeted for deletion.
edgeCases: When the tracked user ID collection is empty, a deleteMany operation is still invoked with an empty ID filter, and the collection remains empty.
If the database deletion rejects, the rejection propagates and the tracked user ID collection is not cleared by the subsequent splice operation.
stateMutations: Mutates the shared userIds collection by removing all elements after successful deletion.
detail.summary: Deletes the users whose identifiers are currently tracked in the shared user ID collection, then clears that collection after successful deletion.

specTests.then: deleteMany is called with where.id.in equal to the tracked IDs, and the tracked collection is empty after the promise resolves.
The rejection propagates and the tracked user ID collection is not cleared by this function.

units.name: createUserWithBookings

detail.name: createUserWithBookings
preconditions: The input contains a user with an email and createdDate accepted by the Prisma user model.
The bookings value is an array of booking property objects accepted by the Prisma nested create operation.
The Prisma client and the shared booking and attendee data are available.
postconditions: A user record is created through prisma.user.create.
One nested booking is requested for each input booking.
Each generated booking receives common booking data and common attendee data unless later spread booking properties override generated fields.
The created user is requested with bookings and credentials included.
The created user's id is appended to userIds.
The returned promise resolves to the created user object returned by Prisma.
invariants: Generated booking numbering is one-based and follows the input bookings order.
Each generated booking initially uses a UID and title derived from the user's email and its one-based position.
The nested booking create operation preserves each input booking's remaining properties through object spreading.
edgeCases: An empty bookings array creates the user with no nested booking creations and still appends the user id to userIds.
Multiple bookings receive distinct position-based default UIDs and titles.
If a booking contains properties that overlap generated fields, the final spread of booking properties overrides the generated values.
If Prisma user creation fails, the rejection propagates and userIds is not appended because the append occurs after the awaited create call.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Invalid input or persistence failures are not handled locally; the async function rejects with the underlying Prisma or runtime error.
